scenarios.name: edge-runtime-turso-client
scenarios.rationale: Both import from @libsql/client/web and pass url and authToken from env, and both say embedded replicas don't work in Workers; A also says outright that the web build supports only remote URLs and rejects file:, and that replicas need a persistent filesystem, which is closer to the rubric, while B gives the reasons (native binding, writable filesystem) but never states the remote-only/no-file: point for the web import.

scenarios.name: atomic-transfer-with-rollback
scenarios.rationale: Both use the db.transaction('write') pattern with positional args, commit, rollback with rethrow, and close in finally; B states the correct 5-second lock timeout and mentions batch as an alternative, while A says roughly 10 seconds (inaccurate against the rubric) but gives a fuller batch example.

scenarios.name: insert-returning-and-duplicate-slug
scenarios.rationale: Both use parameterized db.execute and handle the id correctly; B follows the rubric's primary path exactly (RETURNING id, rows[0], catch LibsqlError and check err.code to map to 409), while A leads with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and only offers the rubric's catch-and-check-code approach (with Number(lastInsertRowid)) as an alternative.
